hypothesis: At very low offered QPS, time-based fixed residency and activation cost rather than saturated service throughput may make one multi-task Generalist operationally preferable to several Heavy Specialists. Sharing is not presumed, and J-only structural shifts must not be replaced by a newly tuned objective.

proposed_design.scope: Separate low-QPS characterization of resident G/S operating states; do not reinterpret the existing 27 contexts or retune them.
proposed_design.frozen_workloads: A separately specified low-QPS/multi-task request schedule must be frozen before GPU observation using the same task mapping; proposed only, no rates selected here.
measurements: idle resident GPU memory with explicit warm state
per-task latency and stable completion under frozen quality constraints
proposed_design.capacity_protocol: Use closed loop only if separately needed for capacity; periodic low offered rate is never g(x).
proposed_design.comparison: Time-based observations must retain separate units and scope from latency J. No silent objective reweighting or fixed-cost term added to Module9.
proposed_design.success: Measured, repeatable fixed-resource/activation tradeoff supports a further explicit fixed-cost research question; it alone does not prove G routing/share benefit under frozen J.
proposed_design.falsification: Fixed Generalist residency/latency/activation cost is larger or no legal SLO/memory window; stop without changing budgets or model pool.
